cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Back My Version
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to remember, repeat, and defend one shared version of events when questions begin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. The allotment committee's asking about the greenhouse. We arrived after the glass broke, remember?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I saw your wheelbarrow hit it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. We came inside afterwards. Can we both tell them we were clearing up?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll say that. I won't lie about the wheelbarrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then start with clearing up. If they ask about the barrow, we moved it away afterwards. Let's both use that order.

mechanism: A teaches its pupil a selective sequence to recruit one defensible shared account while absorbing B refusal to deny the collision.
confusable: Not just approving a one-off excuse: A wants both speakers to remember and repeat the same ordered events under questioning.
comparison: Selective chronology versus coached shared tasting account.
